sections.heading: Malabar Milma: The Dairy Union Headquartered in Kozhikode
paragraphs: The Malabar Regional Co-operative Milk Producers' Union (MRCMPU) was registered on 29 June 1989, began operating on 15 January 1990 and is headquartered in Kozhikode, serving the six northern districts of Kerala. Its own figures for 2025-26 give average procurement of 6,83,143 litres a day from 66,336 farmers and a total processing capacity of 10.75 lakh litres a day.

For a tube buyer this matters because one union operates several plants of different ages, each with its own mix of raw milk reception, pasteurisation, filling and long-life lines, and each replacement job is specified separately.

sections.heading: Kunnamangalam and Naduvattam: The Kozhikode District Plants
paragraphs: Kozhikode Dairy at Kunnamangalam was commissioned on 6 February 1995 with a capacity of 2,00,000 litres a day. MRCMPU lists its market as Kozhikode district plus the Kondotty, Manjeri, Nilambur and Areakode areas of Malappuram, reports a 2025-26 turnover of Rs 430.63 crore, and notes a fully automated ice cream plant of 10,000 litres a day on the site.
The Central Products Dairy at Naduvattam in Kozhikode was commissioned on 4 October 2009 and makes long-life products for the whole union area, with a 2025-26 turnover of Rs 71.13 crore.

sections.heading: Moorkanad Powder Plant and the Wider Malabar Network
paragraphs: Malappuram Dairy at Moorkanad was commissioned on 24 December 2024 at 1,00,000 litres a day with a 10 MT per day spray-drying powder plant. DairyNews reported in January 2021 that the powder plant was planned at Rs 53.93 crore, funded by the State Dairy Development Department, NABARD RIDF and MRCMPU, because Malabar was then procuring 2.12 lakh litres a day more than it could sell as liquid milk.
The union also lists a ₹13 crore UHT line of 40,000 litres a day at Kannur Dairy, imported from Italy and France, and a condensed milk plant with a continuous butter-making unit at Wayanad Dairy.

sections.heading: Choosing a Finish for Malabar Dairy Lines
paragraphs: Ice cream mix, UHT and long-life product lines, and the evaporator feed ahead of a spray dryer are where product residue and CIP cycles are hardest on tube, so we supply 316L to ASTM A270 with an SF4 electropolished bore for them. Each electropolished lot ships with an Ra report and an EN 10204 3.1 certificate traced to the heat number.
Raw milk reception, chilled water and cleaning-solution return lines are usually well served by SF1 or mill-finish 304L, which keeps the budget for the product-contact runs.

sections.heading: What to Send With a Kozhikode Enquiry
bullets: Plant and line: reception, pasteuriser, ice cream, UHT, powder or CIP
Outside diameter and wall thickness, plus total length in metres
Grade and finish required: 316L SF4, 304L SF1 or mill finish
Standard: ASTM A270, A269 or ASME BPE, with any surface roughness limit
Fittings needed: elbows, tees, ferrules or reducers

sections.heading: Delivery to Kozhikode and North Kerala
paragraphs: Orders for Kozhikode travel by road from Mumbai with the electropolished lengths capped at both ends and sleeved, and we confirm the dispatch date and transit in writing once the order is placed. A quotation is sent within 24 hours of a complete enquiry, and every length is checked by PMI before it leaves.
